"one_viewing_summary": "In a residential San Antonio neighborhood, muddy stormwater floods a front yard and reaches
boot height before a cell phone on the porch railing finally receives an emergency flash flood alert. To address this dangerous latency,
UT San Antonio researchers designed a self-powered flood station prototype that harvests ambient light and operates independently of cellular towers. The
station mounts four optical sensors at varying heights along its post to track rising water while auxiliary sensors monitor rain, temperature, humidity
, and light. An integrated TinyML chip processes these environmental readings locally, determining flood risk without contacting an external server.
The station transmits its alert via long-range radio up to a half-mile through city streets or five miles across open
terrain to a central monitoring hub. There, a secondary AI model aggregates station data to project predictive flood inundation maps for emergency responders.
The report concludes by noting that while lab validation reached 98.82% accuracy, no field installations have yet

taken place, leaving deployment as an ongoing goal.",
    "opening_to_ending": "The film opens with
the core vulnerability—delayed cellular emergency warnings while water is already ankle-deep in yards—and systematically demonstrates the mechanical and
computational architecture of UTSA's off-grid alternative. It concludes responsibly by distinguishing lab validation from active municipal deployment,

showing the technician packing the plan alongside the prototype.",
    "verdict": "pass",
    "weakest
_transition": "The transition from Scene 6 to Scene 7 at 40.94s moves from
an indoor command workstation displaying flood routes to an outdoor wooden bulletin board presenting validation figures, relying primarily on color continuity rather than
.800 (s4-event-2), the cutaway into the weatherized station housing clearly shows thin
copper traces routing multimodal sensor data into the glowing TinyML microcontroller, which illuminates the amber risk lamp and increments the risk bar while the distant

server across the street remains disconnected.",
  "verdict": "pass",
  "weakest_frame": "At 00
:51.000 (s8-event-0), the notice board framing is tight on the right

margin where the 'Field result' card rests, though all stamped text remains completely legible and unobstructed."
